rationale: fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained-claude-agentic: val_n=200, seed=42, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.7, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=1.0, dataset_kind=breast_ct, rationale=iter-2 DC-STRENGTH lever, fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained breast val=200. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: iter-1 hr=0.0 (recon PSNR 27.04 dB / RMSE 0.01518 vs 128-view sparse-FBP baseline PSNR 36.32 / RMSE 0.00521 -> ~3x worse, far below floor). (2) Failure mode: the MAYO-trained wavelet prior's baked fd_out_scale=0.05 mis-normalises breast (mu->0.5, 10x), so the flow prior injects mis-scaled structure each Euler step; at dc_relax=0.5 the hard CG data-consistency step only HALF-corrects it back onto the measured sinogram. The prior is actively hurting; the DC anchor is too weak to dominate. (3) ONE KNOB: fd_recon_dc_relax 0.5->1.0 (full CG-projected-image blend), everything else identical to iter-1. (4) HYPOTHESIS: at dc_relax=1.0 the recon leans fully on the CG solve of min||Ax-y||^2 (domain-agnostic, no out_scale mismatch), so RMSE drops toward the sparse-FBP floor and hr may clear 0; if hr stays 0, the mis-scaled prior injected BEFORE each DC-step is structurally poisoning the trajectory (a prior-domain problem, not a DC-strength one), which redirects iters 3+ to init_t / step-count levers that limit prior influence. (5) BUDGET: iter-1 ran well inside 20 min; dc_relax is free. (6) Loop continues; iter-3 on landing.
